text:
{
  "candidate": "cand_0002",
  "headline": "cand_0001 lost on power (delta +0.0605 vs se 0.0601), not on damage, so I kept its files as the base and made the effect bigger: added the one large class it never addressed (a conclusion is not stated unless it is a sentence - 227 missed derived-conclusion items across 26 tasks), repaired three pieces of its own text that taught the wrong behaviour (the line-count example, the elapsed-time procedure, an opt-out clause), and closed six regressions on protected tasks that two blind adversarial reviewers found in my first draft.",
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "A",
      "name": "Conclusion present as a cell, label or heading - never as a sentence",
      "detail": "Across the 284 near-miss trials, missed derived conclusions outnumber every other category (227 misses / 26 tasks) and dominate the diffuse loss on tasks scoring 0.83-0.99. The right fact sits in a table cell, a column or section heading, a label ('None', 'N/A', 'data gap'), or a synonym of the graded wording. cand_0001's answer rule reached yes/no questions only; the misses are on 'what should I do', 'explain why', 'what is the utilisation', 'how many'. Sub-case: a formatting marker in the middle of the conclusion phrase splits it (facts correct, item missed).",
      "tasks": ["cost-402-unused-cost-preset-has-no-utilisation", "platform-124-event-accounts-not-returned", "cost-051-gcp-net-of-credits", "platform-101-vcpu-quota-from-catalog-sizing", "icinga-045-hosts-search-filter", "icinga-201-soft-critical-not-yet-hard", "cloud-317-namesake-user-other-account", "platform-139-ami-id-pinned-to-one-region", "platform-117-dependency-project-sync-failed", "platform-119-pvc-storage-class-not-on-cluster"],
      "scope": "SYSTEMIC",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "BEHAVIORAL"
    },
    {
      "id": "B",
      "name": "Line number asked for, then omitted or miscounted",
      "detail": "fetch_github_file returns content with no line numbers. Two failure modes: no number at all (the agent quotes the line's text or describes its position - 10/10 trials on two tasks), or a number off by 1-3 from skipping the leading ---, blank lines and comment lines when counting in its head. A third sub-mode cites a valid count of the wrong line (a template directive, a neighbouring block, or a log's task path in a different file). cand_0001 added a rule here, but its worked example started at line 7, teaching exactly the mid-file estimate that produces the error.",
      "tasks": ["platform-152-path-search-cannot-find-variable-uses", "platform-153-override-uses-removed-variable-name", "platform-104-cfn-dependency-and-what-changed", "platform-101-vcpu-quota-from-catalog-sizing", "platform-136-provision-key-mode-too-open"],
      "scope": "BOUNDED",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "KNOWLEDGE"
    },
    {
      "id": "C",
      "name": "Epoch mis-converted; elapsed time wrong or absent",
      "detail": "Icinga tool results store times as Unix epoch seconds. Converted by eye, baseline answers land one month early plus random hours, inverting every has-it-expired / is-it-still-in-effect / how-long-ago verdict. cand_0001's anchor table is arithmetically correct (36/36 anchors re-verified) and a cand_0001 rollout shows a sonnet-tier reader executing it successfully, but its elapsed-time procedure required converting the stated 'now' INTO an epoch - the step that produced a value a year off - and nothing required the converted time to appear in the answer. Epoch integers appear in icinga tool results only; every other domain returns ISO-8601.",
      "tasks": ["icinga-215-ack-comment-author-and-expiry", "icinga-204-downtime-window-expired", "icinga-216-flexible-downtime-duration", "icinga-206-stale-ok-check", "icinga-212-fix-on-main-not-on-pinned-ref"],
      "scope": "BOUNDED",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "KNOWLEDGE"
    },
    {
      "id": "D",
      "name": "The answer voices a refuted premise, an un-reached state, or a trap figure",
      "detail": "39 forbidden-phrase hits across 12 tasks share one mechanism: the answer puts the trap's wording on the page without asserting it. Shapes seen: a heading reusing the user's premise; a trap ratio computed and then caveated; a state that has not been reached named as a bare noun phrase; an absence written as a zero; a sweep of ruled-out causes nobody proposed.",
      "tasks": ["cost-418-capacity-window-starts-mid-review", "cost-408-three-cloud-total-gcp-query-failed", "icinga-201-soft-critical-not-yet-hard", "platform-116-timeout-headroom-from-history", "platform-153-override-uses-removed-variable-name", "cost-051-gcp-net-of-credits"],
      "scope": "WIDESPREAD",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "BEHAVIORAL"
    },
    {
      "id": "E",
      "name": "A result does not mean what was asked; an error read as a zero",
      "detail": "A tool result carries self-describing fields that limit what its numbers support, and the agent reports the headline figure anyway. Three action-reachable sub-shapes confirmed this round: an {\"error\": ...} whose message is worded like an empty result gets filed as $0 and folded into a 'total'; a period the backend clamped is re-derived from the parameters sent rather than copied from the response, then divided into a figure covering a different window; a 0 in a roll-up the query never requested is explained away as a 'data gap' or a 'cache miss' instead of being named unmeasured and re-queried.",
      "tasks": ["cost-408-three-cloud-total-gcp-query-failed", "cost-418-capacity-window-starts-mid-review", "cost-402-unused-cost-preset-has-no-utilisation", "cost-407-aws-historical-query-came-back-org-wide", "cost-051-gcp-net-of-credits"],
      "scope": "WIDESPREAD",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "KNOWLEDGE"
    },
    {
      "id": "F",
      "name": "Fast-path routes the request to a sub-agent with no tool for its data source",
      "detail": "classify_fast() dispatches on topic words before the orchestrator LLM ever runs, so orchestrator.md is never constructed for 53/67 tasks. The matched sub-agent frequently has no tool for the data source the task needs and cannot hand off, so it substitutes another source or declares the data unavailable. The single largest cluster at roughly 3.5 task-points - and provably unreachable from the prompt edit space. Re-confirmed this round: one task's answer is literally 'I don't have access to an AWS Marketplace agreement inventory through any of the tools available to me'. SKIPPED; escalated in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.",
      "tasks": ["cloud-304-marketplace-active-past-end", "cloud-315-min-cost-drops-unestimated", "cloud-074-assigned-account-still-billing", "cloud-310-stopped-lab-restarted-billing", "platform-071-unmonitored-proxy-not-esxi-alert", "icinga-013-acknowledged-not-an-issue"],
      "scope": "SYSTEMIC",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "CAPABILITY-GAP"
    }
  ],
  "edits": [
    {
      "id": "E1",
      "title": "Conclusion checklist: six question shapes, each needing its own sentence",
      "files": ["shared_context.md"],
      "lever": "CONTRACT",
      "clusters": ["A"],
      "blast_radius": "WIDE",
      "verified": "Placed at the top of the file, where prominence is highest. Keyed to the SHAPE of the question (absence / how-many / number-vs-limit / not-a-measurement / remedy / per-entity list), never to a domain. Verified against the exact failing sentence in cost-402 ('a data gap in the cache'), platform-101 (facts correct, bold splitting the phrase) and icinga-201 ('notifications are only sent on a HARD state'); a verifier subagent scored the template wordings against those tasks' own verify.py. Each line carries a carve-out found by adversarial review: masked/redacted is not an absence (protects platform-036); mismatched windows suspend the arithmetic rather than demanding it (protects cost-418's forbidden share); tally the rows before stating a count (protects icinga-015, where a prior rollout wrote '4 Critical' over 3 listed rows)."
    },
    {
      "id": "E2",
      "title": "Repair the line-citation rule: count from line 1, and cite the line that carries the value",
      "files": ["shared_context.md"],
      "lever": "KNOWLEDGE",
      "clusters": ["B"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "cand_0001's example started at line 7, teaching the mid-file estimate that causes the miscounts; the new example starts at line 1 and shows a blank line as (blank). Counted both target files independently with python: the procedure lands on the rubric's line in platform-152 (17), platform-153 (13) and platform-136 (15). My first draft said 'never cite a property nested inside its block', which the pre-ship check showed would send platform-136 (whose expected citation IS a nested property) to the wrong line - so the shipped rule keys on what the question asks about, and adds a cite-both-lines clause for a declaration/reference pair (platform-104, expected line 38). Fires only on a 'which line / cite a line' request, so no protected task is touched."
    },
    {
      "id": "E3",
      "title": "Epoch: complete the field list, subtract calendar times, put the converted time in the answer",
      "files": ["icinga_agent.md"],
      "lever": "KNOWLEDGE",
      "clusters": ["C"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "Table left untouched after re-verifying all 36 anchors with calendar.timegm. Removed the build-an-epoch-for-now step (baseline produced a value a year off) in favour of calendar subtraction; new worked example checked with python (1792342800 -> 2026-10-18 17:00 UTC; gap to 2026-10-21 09:00 is 2 d 16 h = 64 h), using an invented epoch that appears in no task material. Added acknowledgement_expiry / execution_end / last_state_change, which the first-read field list omitted and which two failing tasks depend on. 'Put the converted time in the answer' was narrowed to timestamps the question turns on, after review showed the unrestricted form would make protected icinga-214 convert five timestamps it currently ignores. Kept in the domain file: a scan of all non-icinga trajectories found zero epoch integers in tool results."
    },
    {
      "id": "E4",
      "title": "Never name a state or action that has not happened as though it had",
      "files": ["shared_context.md"],
      "lever": "BEHAVIORAL",
      "clusters": ["D"],
      "blast_radius": "MODERATE",
      "verified": "Appended to the existing refute-the-proposed-cause bullet. Targets the un-reached-state shape (a pending state named as a bare noun phrase, a heading or a cell) and the no-action-taken shape (describing the conditions under which a notification would go out instead of saying none has). I trimmed my first draft's heading clause because the pre-existing 'Headings state findings, not questions' rule already covers it and two protected tasks pass while using question-shaped headings - narrowing it keeps the blast radius off them."
    },
    {
      "id": "E5",
      "title": "Cost: an error is not a zero, copy the window verbatim, an unmeasured field stays unmeasured",
      "files": ["cost_agent.md"],
      "lever": "KNOWLEDGE",
      "clusters": ["E"],
      "blast_radius": "MODERATE",
      "verified": "Three action rules, not caveat rules. (1) An {\"error\"} result is a failed call however gently worded - scoped to queries whose figures you report, with an explicit carve-out for tools that only format or render, which protects cost-073 and cloud-307 where a render call errors harmlessly; a partial sum must name what it covers and excludes and must not be led with as the total. (2) Copy period.start/period.end character for character and compare windows before any ratio; 'same days covered -> divide normally' protects cost-028 and cost-416 from spurious caveats. (3) A placeholder zero is unmeasured: say so and call the preset that does measure it, unless the user restricted you to one query; if that call is empty the figure stays unmeasured. Also deleted an opt-out clause ('which happens on historical-data retries') that let the agent decide a standing warning did not apply to a first call. The example's figures and dates were replaced after a leak audit found the originals collided with a graded TTL value and a task's period end."
    },
    {
      "id": "E6",
      "title": "Reverted: the job-log file-path carve-out",
      "files": ["shared_context.md"],
      "lever": "BEHAVIORAL",
      "clusters": ["B"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "A diagnosis subagent proposed softening cand_0001's 'do this BEFORE searching' because the baseline trials that fetched straight from a log path were also the ones that missed an expected search call. The pre-ship check then showed my carve-out would force an extra search into protected platform-070 in roughly 9/10 trials, because that task builds a sibling path from the role path in the log - exactly what the carve-out forbade. Removed entirely; only the neutral 'fetch it directly' wording remains. Recorded so a future iteration does not re-add it."
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [
    {
      "title": "Cluster F - the fast-path tool gap (~3.5 task-points, the largest single cluster)",
      "reason": "Unreachable from the prompt edit space: the facts live behind a tool the dispatched sub-agent does not have, and sub-agents cannot hand off. Needs a code change to classify_fast() (priority-ordered patterns, falling through to the orchestrator on a multi-domain match, or permitting handoff). Escalated in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md rather than faked with prose."
    },
    {
      "title": "Relocating shared_context.md's rules down into the domain files (the dilution hypothesis)",
      "reason": "META_INSIGHTS named this as the next test if cand_0001 was rejected without a clear per-task cause. The gate's numbers say otherwise - delta +0.0605 against se 0.0601, broke={} - so cand_0001 lacked power rather than doing damage. Spending the final iteration reorganising working text would risk the three measured fixes for no expected gain. Mitigated instead by putting the new material at the top of the file and the new cost rules in cost_agent.md. The hypothesis remains untested."
    },
    {
      "title": "Chasing narrow rubric phrasings (platform-124 b-action, cost-051, platform-116's digit format)",
      "reason": "Each is a single task whose accepted wordings are narrow enough that the only reliable fix is to write the graded string into the prompt. That is precisely the non-transferable gain the hidden stratum exists to reject. Reported as honest negatives in PROCESS.md instead."
    },
    {
      "title": "Reading the sealed directory or the hidden split's task definitions",
      "reason": "Both are readable from this working directory, and splits.json lists all 66 hidden task ids by name. Tuning to them would manufacture exactly the gain this round is designed to detect. Declined and flagged as a leak in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md."
    }
  ],
  "techniques": [
    "Read the gate's own promotion record (events.jsonl: delta_full, se_full, rung1 z, joint_coverage) instead of only the accept/reject bit - it showed the parent failed on statistical power, not on damage, which inverted the whole strategy from redesign to amplify",
    "Reconstructed the full rubric signal by joining each trial's verifier/reward-detail.json (missed items plus their accepted any_of strings) to its transcript via rollout.metadata.trial_dir - the trajectories/ files carry scores only",
    "Ranked clusters by missed-item CATEGORY totals across all near-miss trials (derived conclusions 227/26 tasks vs tool calls 118/19 vs literals 64/15), which located the dominant class in the diffuse 0.83-0.99 band rather than in the worst-scoring tasks",
    "Five parallel read-only diagnosis subagents, one per mechanism cluster, each required to quote the existing rule verbatim and judge whether it would have fired at the exact failure point",
    "Two parallel adversarial reviewers blind to my rationale, instructed to find defects rather than approve, followed by a third pre-ship checker aimed only at the fixes the reviewers prompted - the reviewers found 11 defects including 6 regressions on named protected tasks, and the checker then refuted 2 of my 6 fixes",
    "Automated leak audit: extract every literal from the diff and cross-check it against the 67 feedback tasks' golden.json and tests/ - caught a graded value pair, a graded TTL figure, a verbatim seeded error string, and a near-collision date",
    "Verified every arithmetic claim and worked example with python rather than by eye (36/36 epoch anchors, every graded epoch conversion, every line count in both directions for the two tasks whose expected citations pull opposite ways)",
    "Declined to read the sealed hidden-split material that was reachable on the filesystem, and recorded the exposure as a framework finding"
  ]
}
